thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that the memory chip industry has evolved from a fragmented market into a rational oligopoly dominated by three players who collectively maintain stable margins by coordinating capacity and pricing through public announcements rather than illegal collusion. He explains that these companies, including Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix, aim to stay near a 50% market share to avoid regulatory scrutiny and the destructive price wars that occur when one player attempts to aggressively capture market share.
